security_audit.summary: The helper script has real command execution risk because it starts user-supplied server commands with shell=True and runs arbitrary follow-up commands. Most SKILL.md static hits are Markdown formatting false positives, but the skill also discourages source review before script execution.

remediation.suggestion: Replace shell=True with argument lists, separate working directory handling, and an allowlist of approved package manager commands.
Limit the post-ready command to trusted automation scripts or require explicit user confirmation before running it.
Remove language that says not to read source, and instruct agents to review helper scripts before execution.

remediation.issue: Sensitive artifacts in logs or screenshots
remediation.suggestion: Warn users that screenshots and console logs may contain secrets, and write them only to approved output paths.

content.user_title: Test Local Web Apps With Playwright
content.value_statement: Local web apps often fail in rendered states that static review cannot see. This skill guides Playwright automation for screenshots, selectors, logs, and browser checks.
actual_capabilities: Start one or more local servers before running a browser automation command.
Wait for configured localhost ports to become ready before tests continue.
Use Playwright scripts to inspect rendered buttons, links, inputs, and page content.
Capture browser screenshots for visual debugging and regression review.
Capture browser console messages and save them for later review.
Automate static HTML files through file URLs and browser interactions.
limitations: The helper executes local commands and should be used only with trusted project commands.
Examples target localhost and need edits for other ports, routes, or selectors.
It does not provide a complete test runner or assertion framework.
Screenshots and console logs can contain sensitive application data.

use_cases.title: Debug Local UI State
use_cases.description: Inspect rendered controls, screenshots, and console output after a local app starts.

use_cases.title: Verify Feature Flows
use_cases.description: Script browser actions against a running dev server before release.

use_cases.title: Review Static Prototypes
use_cases.description: Open static HTML prototypes and capture before-and-after screenshots.

prompt_templates.title: Open a Local App
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the webapp-testing skill to open my local app at http://localhost:5173, wait for network idle, and describe visible controls.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Logs and Screenshots
prompt_templates.prompt: Start the app command I provide, then capture a screenshot and browser console messages for the main dashboard.

prompt_templates.title: Discover Selectors for a Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the rendered page, list likely selectors for the sign-in flow, then run a Playwright check that uses stable selectors.

prompt_templates.title: Test Multiple Services
prompt_templates.prompt: Start the backend and frontend services, wait for both ports, run a focused browser flow, and summarize failures with evidence.

output_examples.input: Inspect my local dashboard after it starts on port 5173.
output: The dashboard loaded after the server became ready.
Primary controls found: navigation links, dashboard button, and form inputs.
A screenshot was saved for review.

output_examples.input: Capture browser console messages while opening the app.
output_examples.output: The report lists warning and error messages, the action that triggered them, and where the log file was saved.

output_examples.input: Check a static HTML prototype form.
output_examples.output: The result confirms the form opened in Chromium, fields were filled, and final screenshots were captured.

best_practices: Run helper scripts with reviewed, trusted commands only.
Wait for network idle or a stable selector before inspecting dynamic pages.
Store screenshots and logs in approved output locations.
anti_patterns: Do not pass untrusted text directly into server commands.
Do not rely on brittle selectors when role or text selectors are available.
Do not publish screenshots or logs that contain secrets or personal data.

faq.question: Does this skill run real browser automation?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses Python Playwright examples and a helper script for local server workflows.

faq.question: Can it test remote production sites?
faq.answer: It is designed for local web applications. Use production targets only with explicit permission.

faq.question: Does it replace a test framework?
faq.answer: No. It helps create focused browser checks, but it does not manage test suites.

faq.question: Can it collect console logs?
faq.answer: Yes. The console logging example captures browser messages and writes them to an output file.

faq.question: Why is command execution a security concern?
faq.answer: The server helper starts commands supplied by the user, so only trusted commands should be used.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
